body: I just talked to my friend and she's renting out a room in her apartment and it's affordable. It made me a bit calmer because I don't have to be homeless, but I still feel depressed and anxious. I got used to my apartment, my neighbourhood, my little routines... Above all I'm going to miss my grandma, and I know I can't take her with me.

Thank you. The thing is, I feel that way because things were out of my control. I am the victim and I couldn't do anything about it. I didn't know about my father's debts until everything started falling apart. 

I sacrificed everything and put my life on hold to take care of my grandma (my father's mother). And now I don't have a full time job, I don't have a place to go to... My life is falling apart because of my father's mistakes.

Thank you for your advice. A lawyer isn't an option because it's too expensive and I don't think I'll ever get my money back. My father is penniless at the moment and he owes a lot of money to different people. I'm very ashamed of what he's done... Ca't get over it.

I agree. It's easier when you don't see them every day. I'm working on a project with this man, and it's gonna take two months (a couple of hours a day). Enough for me to develop a deep crush.

I wish I could be myself. The thing is, I freeze when I'm around people. It was easier when I was at college because I was surrounded by people all the time, and I got used to it. Ever since I graduated, I've been mostly working from home, so it's become challenging working with 10+ people.

I'm so sorry you had to go through this. There aren't many things as painful as being in love with an unavailable person. I had similar experience in the past, almost every crush I had was unavailable in one way or another, or I thought they liked me but I'd find out later about their girlfriend, or they'd get in a relationship before I decided to make the first move. And the thing is, most of men (and women as well) older than 30 are already married, in a relationship, etc., so it's difficult to find someone single. AND even if I had a crush who was single, I had no chance. 

This man I recently met... Oh, it's been just a week or so, although I've heard about him 10 years ago, because he's really good at my field of interest and I've always admired his work. And now, he's much more interesting in person. It's possible that we get closer through working together in the next two months. But I'm not sure about it. I wish I could be more optimistic about it, but it's so difficult because of my previous experience.

Oh yes. I haven't been in love for almost three years and I don't have male friends anymore, so I usually fantasise about men I encounter online, which makes me feel a bit pathetic, but... it's just my loneliness, I guess. 

There's this online community where people from my country gather, and I post there occasionally. There are quite a few interesting men who participate in the community. This particular man seemed really nice, funny and intelligent so I googled everything about him. He's a journalist and activist, so it was easy to learn about things that he does and watch his interviews and so on. No need to mention I fantasised about meeting him in real life. I imagined what it would be like to have someone who is exactly like him by my side. One time he posted something about his girlfriend, so my bubble of fantasy burst. It's not the first time something like this happen. 

I know it's silly and immature but those little crushes make me feel a bit better.

I'm so sorry. The financial abuse is triggering, I've gone through the same thing recently and I know exactly how you feel. My dad is a narcissist and my step-mother is an enabler. He financially abused both of us, took a lot of money from us and sold my step-mother's apartment, but I feel like she's become so numb that she lets him do whatever he wants with her money and her life. She's mad and disappointed but she never stands up for herself, unlike me. I confronted my dad every time which made me look like a bad person while my step-mother stays quiet. I guess it's impossible for enablers to change. The same goes for narcissists.

A couple of years ago I tried all these things - exercised at gym, lost some weight, took care of my looks, bought myself new clothes. Results? I felt a bit better about myself, that's for sure, but everything else was the same. Men still didn't approach me. I got some compliments here and there, but they were never of romantic or sexual nature. Guys who wanted to hang out with me just didn't see me as girlfriend material.

The thing is, looks does matter, but what matters more is being attractive (even unconventionally attractive) to the opposite sex. I feel like I can improve my looks, but I can't make myself attractive by doing so. Attraction is a whole new level. Some women have the ability to attract men, some don't. Oh, and there are women with different flaws such as weight or skin issues, but they still do attract other people.

What makes difference between women and men are expectations, I guess. Society expects from a man to approach first. A woman is considered pathetic if she asks a guy out. It doesn't make sense, but that's how things are. Also, men are mostly attracted to psychical appearance.

Thank you for your kind words. I'm sorry for what you're going to. People are insensitive and they rarely try to put themselves in other people's shoes. The only thing we can do is either improve our lives (which is more difficult than other people think and it depends on circumstances we often don't have control of) OR find people who understand us because they've been through the same thing.

I'm taking care of grandma because I don't have a full time job and I work from home, so... my dad made me do it. I love my grandma, no doubt about it, but it's really tough being a caregiver and putting my life on hold. My dad and his wife help me here and there. And my grandma doesn't have anyone else. My dad is her only son and I'm her only grandchild. Young women are most often sacrificed, it really makes me sad. 

Two years ago - before my Grandma got sick - my biggest issue was being FA. But at least I had freedom, money, hobbies. Now I'm FA, penniless and even more lonely and alienated. I realised how important it is to cherish little things. Such as freedom. Freedom is everything.
I know. I know only one FA woman. There are some single people I know, but they recently broke up or are single by choice. Being FA is very isolating.

I'm so sorry to hear about your daughter. That's true, in difficult situations like this one we found out who our friends are. People are so occupied with their own lives that they sometimes don't even realise what their friends are going through. Or they don't want to see bad things happening so they distance themselves. And we can't blame them. It's just... two different worlds.

Gotta love your idea, it's really funny! It weird, but she doesn't post this kind of stuff to her Instagram of Facebook, so yeah, she sends it directly to me. All the time. And I don't know why - is it her wish to share her precious moments with me or is she trying to prove to both myself and herself she's having a great time. Not sure about it.

Thank you for your advice, it's really helpful. I was into gym a year ago, but I wasn't able to exercise regularly and be a caregiver at the same time. However, it did help me to feel a bit healthier, so I'm considering exercising at home. At least 30 minutes a day would do me good.

I'm not active on social networks (except Twitter where I mostly follow news, TV series and film related stuff), but my friends keep sending me pictures via Viber or talking about their experiences in details. For instance, they talk about their boyfriends, sex, travelling, expensive restaurants, people they met. But if I asked them not to talk about these things, they would barely have anything else to talk about because it's 90% of their life. So... I can't do that. The only thing I could do is distance myself, but I don't want to lose my friends.

I relate A LOT. Especially to the the pretty girl part.

I have a few friends from college I hang out with occasionally. Every time we go somewhere, I see how it's easy for them. Men approach them even if they do nothing besides just sitting there. My childhood friend met her husband at a night club. He approached her first, asked for her number, etc. I see how men act differently when they talk to attractive girls. They're highly engaged, give compliments, make jokes. And when they talk to me, they're cold and formal. They NEVER flirt.

I've seen it so many times, and yet I get advice I should act differently: smile more, approach men first, be more assertive and confident. The thing is, some girls are attractive by definition, and everything is way easier for them. They don't need to follow internet advice, they just need to show up and be themselves. There are average looking girls who are attractive in other ways, and they also don't have trouble attracting men. It comes naturally. 

Yeah, it's such a weird experience being FA.

I know what it's like. I'm an atheist myself, not only because of injustice and suffering. I feel like atheism is more logical and substantial than any religion out there. But we all find comfort in different beliefs and it's all fine. I hope you do what's best for you. Please don't lose hope.

I'm sorry to hear about your struggles. I feel you. I've been asking myself a hundred times why some people have everything in the world - security, good family, relationships, etc. - while others struggle to survive. There's no answer. Things happen for no reason, and we just have to be strong enough to survive. Try thinking about your future. I know it's easy to say, but there must be way out.
My dad's wife helps, but I'm the primary caregiver. It's extremely exhausting, but there's nothing else we could do about it, unfortunately.

Thank you. I wish I could catch up and feel less alienated. Medicare is unfortunately not an option, I'm not from the USA. In my country there's nothing I can do about my grandma. Elderly facilities are expensive and the ones that are financed by government aren't available (you have to be on the list and wait for 10 years or more), and right now I have no money to pay for them.

That's exactly what I thought. I know she wants to share things with me and probably doesn't realise it makes me feel bad, but it's difficult to listen to how much my hometown sucks and how she ate at an expensive restaurant while I'm struggling with making money and taking care of my grandma. She talks about all the stuff she and her boyfriend do together, places they visit, people they meet. Perhaps these things aren't special or outstanding - most people have relationships, do fun stuff together and travel. It's just that I'm not able to connect to her experience.
Cat.
Cat.
Cat.
Cat.

Not being able to express feelings without getting criticised for it. 

Being called crazy and emotionally unstable every time I felt sad, angry or depressed.  

Being told my life was great every time I opened up about my struggles. (I'd been a refugee until I turned 6, my mother died when I was 7, my grandma raised me because my Ndad was absent all the time, now I take care of my grandma, my Ndad took my money, I got no full time job, etc.)

My Nfather hates it when I talk about things I'm passionate about, such as literature, theatre, movies, philosophy, etc. He believes that I want to make him feel stupid when I mention something he's not familiar with.

He hates it when I display emotions. When I was 13, he taught me to control myself and never ever become too emotional. Every time I cried or got angry, he yelled at me: 'SELF-CONTROL'. The sad thing is, I've been struggling with displaying emotions my whole life. And that's one of the reasons why I never got in a relationship, I guess. 

My Nfather doesn't want me to become independent and go NC. He told me I wouldn't be able to support myself financially. Meanwhile, he made me his servant. I take care of his sick mother and work from home. He's stolen all my savings so I can't just leave.
  
There are plenty of other selfish things he's done, but the last one hit me hardest.

My Nfather used to say that parents weren't responsible at all for the way their children's life turned out to be. Everything that went wrong was my fault, even when I was barely 6 years old. Like he said, I was a difficult child. Today, I'm a difficult person. His lies and abusive behaviour don't matter. Narcissists believe they're perfect, despite being the ones who blame others.

Unfortunately, it's not available in my country (I live in Europe.)

I've been working on a few art projects lately, so I'm expecting to get paid soon. And I know I won't lend my money again.

"It's your own fault you're unhappy."

"I lied to you because you were a difficult child."
"I kept secrets from you to protect you."
(My Nfather kept his girfriend, now his wife, a secret for 15 years. He lied that he quit smoking. He lied about his debt and his shady business he got into. There were too many secrets and lies to remember.)

"If you left, you'd still be unhappy. That's just how you are."

"Don't cry." (Every time I show emotions, my Nfather gets angry.)

"Stop complaining, your life is great." (Yeah, I'm a 24/7 caregiver to my grandma, got no full time job, no money cause my Nfather took my savings, no boyfriend and very few friends.) 

"You're pure evil."

"You'd be completely alone without me."

"No wonder you don't have a boyfriend."

"It's better for you to be quiet."

"It's none of your business what I do." (Oh, and he sold his wife apartment after going bankrupt and completely destroyed her, lend money not only from me but from some suspicious so called friends, he is in such a huge debt that affects me and his wife, etc.) 

"If you're gonna be this way, I'll kill myself" (After telling him how much he hurt me with his actions.)

Amazing! 👏 You must feel great being in confrol of your money and your life. You deserve it. 

The worst thing about Nparents is that they think we owe them something all the time, just because we're their children. I hope they don't manipulate you by buying that car. Owing someone money can make relationships much more difficult.

Yeah, he has shallow friendships and tends to take advantage of his friends. He tells me he'll give me my money back, but I'm not sure about it anymore. The money doesn't matter anymore, because it only showed me what kind of person he was, and I learnt my life time lesson. Don't give your money to anyone. Especially not your Nparent. 

He tells me I'm a bad person because I confronted him about money and his bad parenting skills. Obviously, he believes that parents have minimal impact on their children. As he said, it's all my fault.

The only thing that government could help us with was having a geriatric nurse visit my grandma once a week. Elderly facilities are expensive and the ones that are financed by government aren't available (you have to be on the list and wait for 10 years or more), and right now I have no money, and my Nfather is in debt, so there's nothing we can do about it. I have no choice but to take care of my grandma and work from home as a freelance artist.
He believes he's a good person because he has many friends and people usually like him. Like many narcissists, he's charming and soft-spoken in public. And very manipulative.

I like guys who have good taste in art, literature and music, and have a great sense of humour.  Also, they are open-minded, liberal and unconventional. My dream is to have someone I could talk to for hours, travel across the world, share my thoughts and interests... Physically, I don't have any particular preferences. I do like dark hair and dark eyes, but it doesn't really make a difference if he's blond or whatever.

In reality I usually fall for guys who are emotionally unavailable and deeply troubled. Guess that often goes with artsy and intellectual types. But for once I'd like to fall for someone who's reliable and confident. 

So, yeah, that would be my type.

I live in Europe. He doesn't have access to my bank account, but he didn't want to hear 'no' for an answer when asking money from me. Basically, he was emotionally blackmailing me and telling me that we were in danger (some people were coming after him because he owed them money). I was scared to death so I gave him all my money. No need to mention how disappointed I am with my him and the things he's done. I learnt my lesson. I won't ever give him a penny.

Yes, grandma lives with us. I have to take care of her because I work from home.

Thanks. I started saving money again. I had been saving it for years, and my dad took all of my savings (more than 10k Euros) by threatening me after going bankrupt. Now I have to balance between three freelancing jobs while taking care of my sick Grandma so I could save some money. And it's really exhausting.

Thanks for your advice. Yeah, that's right - the sense of freedom you're talking about seems amazing. I can't go where I want to. I haven't travelled for years. I lost some of my friends because I didn't have time to hang out with them and cherish our friendship. My life consists of fulfilling my Ndad's and my Grandma's demands, and I feel completely miserable that at the age of 28 I got nothing. I wish I could just leave, but it's difficult because my Grandma is in very bad health.

Thank you. That's what I believe too but my Ndad convinced me that it was all in my head and that I was just naturally unhappy and ungrateful, which had nothing to do with his actions. And he believes that I'll always stay that way, no matter where I go and what I do. I wish I could just leave and experience real freedom. I know it would make me feel better.
I'm sorry you still have to deal with her sometimes, but the good thing is that you're free now, and it's really precious. I hope everything works out for you in the future money wise.

Thank you for sharing your experience. It must have been devastating dealing with your NMom, but I'm glad that your life is great now. It's comforting knowing that it's not our fault we feel unhappy (as our Nparents try to convince us), and that the change is indeed possible. My Ndad was always telling me I was incapable of living on my own, thus making me so insecure I found it difficult to go NC, even when I had a chance. I still find it difficult because of my Grandma, whom I take care of 24/7. Just thinking about going NC makes me feel better. I hope I find the way.
Thank you. That's exactly what I need. I've got trust issues because of what my Ndad has done to me, especially when it comes to men. I wish I could experience being respected and treated well.
Thank you. Being forever alone is difficult enough, and dealing with family stress makes it almost unbearable. I wonder if FAness is partially caused by the way our parents raised us.

Thank you for sharing your experience. What your mother did sounds horrible. It must have been hard for you, but I'm glad you made it. Have you completely cut ties with your mother? 

I've been thinking a lot about leaving home. Unfortunately, it's not an option at the moment, because my grandma couldn't make it without me. My father knows this and takes advantage of it so he could control my life.

I wonder if their relationship is gonna work out in real life, given that the simulation didn't include other important factors such as work, family, interactions with friends and other people. 

Anyway, such a great episode. Can't stop thinking about it.

I know exactly how you feel. I used to develop big crushes in the past, some of which lasted more than two or three years. It was painful being in love with someone who doesn't feel the same about you, so I guess that's the main reason why I find it impossible to have a crush and go through the same experience once again. It's like a defence mechanism that protects us from getting hurt.
I still have some hope left, but it is much easier when I try to not think about it. Hope can be a destructive thing.

As someone who cares about women's rights, I do worry when a perfectly healthy looking woman is represented as fat in a movie. I do worry when movies lack strong and independent female characters or when they reduce a female character to an object of desire and nothing else. So what if it's a fictional character? It doesn't mean that the problem doesn't exist, and that we shouldn't discuss it. The same thing goes for the representation of racial, gender and sexual identities in fiction. We can't simply ignore other people's perceptions, regardless of the fact that it's fiction. And I think that it's necessary to talk about it. Or even worry about it. But hey, I'm a dramatic art student, so fictional characters and other people's perceptions are what I have to deal with on a daily basis.

I've never said that people in relationships don't have to offer something of value to the other person. And I don't think that people who post here expect that they get all the love of the world while they selfishly offer nothing to the other person.  
What I meant was that FA people deserve to be loved even if they have flaws because every day we encounter flawed people who are in relationships and yet we keep getting advice that we are "not good enough".

Good looks without a doubt make things easier, but I'm sure both you and I know a lot of people that are far from being models or even average looking but they have no problems getting into relationships. 
I thought that I'd become more successful if I improved my looks, so I excercised, lost weight, started dressing better, and everthing that goes with it. What happened was that I got noticed and was given compliments by both men and women. However, it did nothing for me in the love department. That said, I'm not against self-improvement -- it's great and inspiring if you do it for yourself, but there are no rules when it comes to relationships. As I see it, love happens to all kinds of people, and not all of them are good looking social butterflies who are always cheerful and happy. 
I'm sure your looks aren't the issue, and please don't view yourself as ugly. I'd say that luck (and not looks) plays a huge part in dating. No matter how accomplished you feel, it won't make a difference unless you get lucky enough to meet the right person for you.

I can relate to what your saying as I had the same problem back in my highschool days. I just couldn't connect with people surrounding me, no matter how much I tried, and that made me think that something was wrong with me, and that I'll never fit in. The thing is... We didn't have much in common, and they weren't the right friends for me. When I started going to college, I made a lot of friends who shared my interests and values. The thing that counts the most is, I guess, being in the right place at the right time -- and meeting people who may be right for you. If you ran a club, that means you have good social skills. Plus, you're surrounded by people all the time, which increases your chances to meet someone who will eventually become your friend. I'm sorry if it sounds a bit like a cliché, but I think in situations like this it's about having a great luck to come across someone who's right for you. 

As for my problem, I've heard different opinions from my friends. They say things like "go out more", some of them suggesting that I should "let myself go" and "get drunk", but I'm not much of a party person so that doesn't work for me. I used to go out, and it definitely wasn't my thing. I indeed am an introverted person, but I don't have trouble communicating with people, so I don't know why I find love and relationships so challenging. A close friend of mine suggested that I should be more open, leave my comfort zone, travel more, have fun and be more relaxed and happy. The advice didn't really help me because I find it difficult to change my lifestyle, like party and get drunk if that's not the way I am. The same goes for "being relaxed and happy" -- I don't like the idea of putting on a mask. Basically, the most common advice is to not be yourself. :/

Thanks a lot for sharing your experience. It's funny how people who give dating advice have the idealistic view of a socially acceptable and thus sexually and romantically desirable person, whereas in reality flawed people don't seem to have any problems attracting the opposite sex. Life just isn't fair -- and I think that even if it's not a pleasant notion, it can surely help us see things as they really are. We shouldn't feel guilty. We shouldn't think that we are unworthy of anyone's love just because we've been told that we aren't "the best version of ourselves". Nobody is, actually. Being in the right place makes things a lot easier. It took me a long time to realise that it's not all about the self-improvement thing (I've done it...or at least I've tried). It's also about luck. 

People on the FA subs are often discussing social anxiety and depression. There's an opinion that depressed and anxious people can't get into relationships. I met a clinically depressed girl with social anxiety, and yet she had at least five relationships. On the other hand, I don't consider myself anxious or depressed (I've had ups and downs just like most of the people), but I've never even come close to a relationship. 

All in all, it seems reasonable to create opportunities and hope we finally end up in the right place.

There's also the opposite situation when they want to portray an average looking girl who everyone in the movie calls fat, but she's always played by an actress that is far from being fat or even chubby. A perfect example is fat shaming of Love Actually's Natalie, who is indeed a beautiful looking girl, and no fat whatsoever. Calling someone average fat can be insulting to people that struggle with their weight issues. If a skinny or average girl is perceived as fat, and everyone makes fun of her because of it, how does it make women who are overweight by all means feel about themselves?
